stemBlocks.value: A cuboid has length 12 cm, width 9 cm and height 8 cm. AC is a diagonal of the base and AG is a space diagonal. a) Calculate the length of AC. b) Hence calculate the length of AG. c) State why Pythagoras' theorem may be used twice in this problem.
Think first: Get the flat base diagonal first — it becomes one leg of a second, upright right-angled triangle.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p170-q03 from workbook page 170.

solutionSteps.instruction: Work in the rectangular base ABCD.

contentBlocks.value: AB = 12 cm and BC = 9 cm meet at right angles

solutionSteps.instruction: Set up the upright triangle ACG.

contentBlocks.value: CG is the vertical edge of 8 cm and it is perpendicular to the base, so ∠ACG = 90°
Result: legs AC = 15 cm and CG = 8 cm
Two separate right-angled triangles exist: ABC lying flat in the base, and ACG standing upright because the vertical edge is perpendicular to every line in the base
Result: two right angles, so two applications

strategyBlocks.value: Apply Pythagoras in the horizontal base to find AC, then again in the vertical triangle ACG using AC and the height.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) AC = 15 cm  (b) AG = 17 cm  (c) Because the solid contains two different right-angled triangles: ABC in the horizontal base (adjacent edges of a rectangle meet at 90°), and ACG in a vertical plane (the edge CG is perpendicular to the base, so it is perpendicular to AC). Pythagoras applies once in each.

whyThisWorks.value: A vertical edge of a cuboid is perpendicular to every line drawn in the base, so pairing it with any base line automatically creates a right-angled triangle. That is what lets a three-dimensional length be reached in two flat steps: reduce the base to a single diagonal, then stand that diagonal up against the height. The same idea gives AG² = 12² + 9² + 8².

commonErrors.misconception: Trying to use the height together with a single edge, skipping the base diagonal step.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Trying to use the height together with a single edge, skipping the base diagonal step.

commonErrors.misconception: Using 12 and 8 in the second step instead of AC = 15 and 8.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Using 12 and 8 in the second step instead of AC = 15 and 8.

commonErrors.misconception: Treating AG as a face diagonal rather than a space diagonal.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Treating AG as a face diagonal rather than a space diagonal.

examTip.value: For any cuboid, the space diagonal is √(l² + w² + h²) — use the two-step method to show working, then use this formula to check your answer.
